fixed: The express man walked past behind the crate, so only his head showed over it and he looked like the man in the box. He now walks up beside the crate and stops to look at it.
Henry wore a white shirt, and in every close-up the white captions lay on it and were hard to read. His shirt is green.
The children stood behind the wagon with their legs showing under it. The wagon bed is slung low between its wheels, so they read as standing in it.
The owner laughed in his close-up and pointed with his arm against Henry's chest. He keeps a cold half smile and folds his arms.

The folded man's knee poked out through the top of the crate, his hand lay over the painted words, and his black limbs were lost against the dark inside. The crate is a little taller, the hand is on the boards, and the inside is a lighter brown.
notes: The crate stands out in the open on a dark red plain under a moon. The script asks for darkness, with the sound of wheels and an engine outside; the studio has no ship's hold or freight car yet.
His head is on the lid with his body doubled over above it. The face is turned about three quarters of the way over, not fully upside down, so it can still be read.
The swollen veins are shown with the red throbbing mark the style uses on a head, beside his temple.
The title ribbon touches the top of the crate in the opening shot. No face is under it.
No rain falls in the pictures; there is the sound of rain under the road scene. The street is the village street in dark blue-gray, with a moon.
Nancy is not drawn pregnant. She and the others in the line wear wrist chains and walk upright; nobody is shown hurt.
The wagon has no horse: its pole runs off toward the edge of the picture. In the child's close shot the two younger children are cut by the edges of the frame.
The coin passes from Henry's hand to the owner's as the two hands meet; one person handing a thing to another is not built as a move of its own.
Nancy walks on behind the rope while Henry stops at the first post. The line does not shrink into the distance; the last picture is Henry's face.
Two shots are short on purpose: On purpose (1.7 s) and Father! Father! (about 2 s with its pause).

The voices: the narrator at a slower pace, the child in the bright woman's voice (there is no child's voice), and a new steadier man's voice saved for Henry, who first speaks in part 3. The heartbeat and the rain are two new sounds. Claude cannot hear; the listening is Biku's.
